headline: Highest risk is data leakage: aci can egress broadly and touch CRM/email data, while dagster is local-only with no filesystem or network access, making prompt-injection and capability-conflict pathways mostly blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP/direct function calls and may ingest external content, but dagster has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surface, so there is no documented automatic bridge. Any injection would require unusual manual transfer or an external orchestrator not shown here.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies aci output into a dagster task definition or config, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external MCP server is introduced between them, the pathway changes materially.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into task specs.
Require human review before any dagster job consumes aci text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so sensitive data can leave its boundary. dagster itself has no network egress or file access, which reduces pairwise leakage, but if aci forwards data into dagster-managed pipelines the blast radius includes multiple work products and sensitive records.
conditions: IF aci sends CRM or email content into a dagster pipeline, leakage risk increases.
IF dagster is later configured with file or network access, the pairwise boundary weakens.
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive fields.
Block CRM/email payloads from being passed into dagster.
Review outbound destinations used by aci.
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on inter-agent handoffs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API calls, but dagster is documented with no filesystem write, no git modification, no subprocesses, and no network egress. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so a write-write conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF dagster is reconfigured to write the same shared directory or git repo, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep dagster read-only in this pairing.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Do not grant dagster git write access.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and dagster is an orchestrator, so a plausible chain is aci-produced output feeding dagster jobs without verification. dagster is not documented here as critically evaluating upstream content, so the pair can propagate mistaken facts into downstream workflows.
conditions: IF dagster consumes aci-generated text or parameters without validation, errors can cascade.
IF aci is used to draft operational instructions for dagster jobs, downstream actions may amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before dagster execution.
Require schema checks on aci outputs.
Limit aci to draft-only recommendations.
requires-engineering: add automated approval gates for dagster-triggering payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and support data and has broad network egress, while dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator with no stated residency or retention controls. The pair can therefore move regulated customer data into an environment whose compliance posture is unspecified, creating a likely policy mismatch rather than a provable residency violation.
conditions: IF customer or support data includes regulated personal data, compliance review is required.
IF dagster pipelines retain or log those records, retention mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Exclude regulated records from aci-to-dagster flows.
Document retention for both systems.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows across both tools.
